rejected_spans: `attempt()` converts a thrown exception, and only a thrown exception, per its own doc comment in [src/lib/result.ts](../../../src/lib/result.ts). The Supabase client does not throw on a permission denial or a missing row; it returns `{ data: null, error }`. So wrapping the call in `attempt()` and reading only what comes back would let a denial arrive as a success carrying `null`, which Zod would then reject as `response_malformed`.
Three named kinds, three real causes, rather than one misleading one.

Without task 10's check, a denial here looks the same in all three cases, and the switch would read as permanently engaged while every visible signal looked exactly as designed.
